Two-panel academic figure for a TOP venue paper (CoRL/NeurIPS). Double-column width, aspect ratio ~2.5:1, figsize (14, 5.5) inches, 300 DPI, white background.

Panel (a) 'Training Setup' (left, ~55% width):
A vertical architecture diagram showing the training pipeline of a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with auxiliary spatial supervision.

Bottom to top flow:
1. INPUT BOX: 'RGB Observation' — light gray fill (#F0F4F8), subtle gray border (#95A5A6), rounded corners 8px, fontsize 12pt bold
2. SPLIT into two encoder boxes (side by side):
   - Left: 'DINOv2' with subtitle '1024-d patches' — light blue fill (#EBF0F7), blue border (#4C72B0), rounded corners 8px
   - Right: 'SigLIP' with subtitle '1152-d patches' — light blue fill (#EBF0F7), blue border (#4C72B0), rounded corners 8px
   - Thin elegant arrows from RGB up to both encoders
3. Between encoders and LLM: italic gray annotation 'concat (2176-d)'
4. LLM BOX: 'LLM Backbone' with subtitle 'Llama-2 7B + LoRA' — warm cream fill (#F5F0E8), brown border (#937860), wider than encoder boxes
   - Arrows from both encoders converging into LLM
5. From LLM, two outputs split upward:
   - LEFT: 'Action Head' with subtitle '7-DoF tokens' — light green fill (#E8F5E9), green border (#55A868)
     - Above it: green bold label 'L_action' with small arrow pointing down
   - RIGHT: 'Aux Head' with subtitle 'BEV / Depth' — warm orange fill (#FFF3E0), orange border (#E69F00)
     - Above it: orange bold label 'lambda(t) * L_aux' with small arrow pointing down
     - Small red-outlined badge 'BN/LN' near the Aux Head (indicating normalization choice)
6. KEY ELEMENT: A dashed red arrow from Aux Head back down to LLM backbone, with annotation 'gradient flow?' in red italic bold inside a light pink rounded box (#FFF0F0, red border #C44E52). This represents the critical experimental variable.
7. Above Aux Head: gray italic annotation 'discarded at inference' in a light yellow box (#FFF8E1), with thin gray arrow pointing down to Aux Head

Arrow style: thin, elegant, small arrowheads (not bulky). Color-coded to match source box borders.

Panel (b) 'Factorial Design' (right, ~45% width):
A 2x2 grid showing the experimental factorial design.

Column headers (above grid): 'Gradient ON' in red (#C44E52) bold, 'Gradient OFF' in purple (#8172B3) bold
Row headers (left of grid): 'BN' and 'LN' in dark text (#2C3E50) bold, fontsize 13pt

Four cells in the 2x2 grid:
- Top-left (BN x ON): 'Full OCC' — light red background (#FDECEA), red text (#C44E52), bold, with red border
- Top-right (BN x OFF): 'Detach OCC' — light purple background (#EEEBF5), purple text (#8172B3), bold, with purple border
- Bottom-left (LN x ON): 'Full OCC+LN' — light orange background (#FFF5E0), orange text (#E69F00), bold, with orange border
- Bottom-right (LN x OFF): 'Detach+LN' — light brown background (#F3EDE6), brown text (#937860), bold, with brown border

Grid border: thin gray (#BDC3C7), rounded corners. Internal dividers: thin gray lines.
Each cell: rounded inner box with colored fill and colored border matching text color.

Below grid, labeled 'Additional:' in bold:
Four small colored square markers with labels arranged in two rows of two:
- Green (#55A868) square: 'Random OCC'
- Blue (#64B5CD) square: 'Cutoff / Reverse'
- Yellow (#CCB974) square: 'Depth-only'
- Navy (#4C72B0) square: 'Vanilla (no aux)'

Below that, gray italic text: '5 factors across 12 conditions: gradient flow / label content / normalization / reference frame / temporal extent'

Panel labels: '(a)' and '(b)' in 15pt bold at top-left of each panel.

STYLE REQUIREMENTS:
- Publication quality for a TOP venue (CoRL/NeurIPS)
- Elegant, premium, sophisticated — NOT cheap or homework-like
- Subtle drop shadows (2px, 10% opacity) on boxes
- Rounded corners (8px) on all rectangles
- Thin, elegant arrow heads — not bulky matplotlib defaults
- Serif font (Times New Roman or Liberation Serif) for all text
- Muted, harmonious color palette — NO saturated primary colors
- Generous white space between elements
- Consistent visual weight across both panels
- NO matplotlib default styling: no gray background, no thick gridlines, no tab10 colors
